references.text: The same theme of distinguishing between the unclean and the clean, between animals that may be eaten and those that may not
Reiterates the command to distinguish between holy and common, and between clean and unclean, in the context of Israel's holiness
Ezekiel describes the priests' duty to teach the people the difference between holy and common, between unclean and clean
The prophet accuses the priests of failing to distinguish between holy and common, and of making no distinction between unclean and clean
The immediate context for the verse: the prohibition against wine and strong drink for priests when they enter the tabernacle
Peter's letter quotes Leviticus on holiness and calls believers to be holy in all their conduct
